# tools

Test tooling, not shipped.

`sweep.py` is the mutant sweep: each mutant removes one check, and the tests must fail at an assertion. Its rules are at the top of the file; `docs/FREEZE-v1.md` says how to read a result. Run it from any folder, on a build node with Rust stable, Node 22 and Python 3.12, one job and its own cargo target: `python3 -I tools/sweep.py` for all of them (some hours on 4 CPUs, 8 GiB; `@format` alone is about 70 minutes), or `python3 -I tools/sweep.py <name> …` for some, where a name can be a part of the list: `@format`, `@verbs`, `@both`, `@fidelity`, `@merge`, or the bridge's `@bridge-rows` (`@bridge-report-a`, `@bridge-report-b`, `@bridge-pack`), `@bridge-parse` and `@bridge-run`. Split the list across jobs if one would run too long. It edits the checkout's sources while it runs and puts them back, so don't run it in a checkout you're working in. Read the `mutants result:` and `needs a look:` lines, not only the exit code. Its exit: 0 when every mutant held, and only then does it print `mutants finished`; 1 for names it doesn't know or parts that don't add up; 2 when a control run (the tests with no mutant) failed; 3 when no mutant ran; 4 when one needs a look (a survivor, a stale pattern, a build that failed, a failure at no line that counts). `catch.verdict` gives the last three, and its self-test holds them. A wrapper treats any exit but 0 as a failure.

**What counts as a catch** is written in `catch.py`, and `python3 -I tools/test_catch.py` is its self-test. A failing line counts when it's in test code, under `crates/board/tests/` or in a unit test's `#[cfg(test)]` module in library source, and it's an assert macro (`[assert]`), an `expect_err` with a string literal (`[expect_err]`), a `panic!` whose first argument is a literal, which may start on the next line (`[panic]`), or an `expect` whose literal starts `check:`, a test's own stated check that a call succeeds (`[check]`). In `tests/support/` only an assert or a `check:` message counts, since helpers are mostly setup. A plain `expect`, `unwrap`, an index, arithmetic, a message that isn't a literal, and library source outside a test module don't count. A failure is read against the run's own source: the mutated file's text, kept from before the restore, and every other file as it is (`catch.run_lines`), so a mutant that adds or removes lines can't move a catch. As a backstop, a sweep refuses to start with a mutant that changes the line count of a Rust file holding test code (`catch.moves_test_lines`), naming it. A mutant is caught if the first failure or any other failing test counts; `CAUGHT` names the kind, and each `FAILS` line says what counts there or why it doesn't. A script's or the JavaScript checker's own `FAILED` line is its catch (`[script]`) when it names the planted case before a colon, `FAILED <case>: …`; a bare `FAILED` line doesn't count.

`fuzz/` holds cargo-fuzz targets for the decoders: JSON, `board.json`, packages, raw ops and verbs. It's its own workspace, so a normal build never pulls libFuzzer, and it's test tooling, never shipped. Build on a node with nightly Rust and `cargo-fuzz`. A violated property in `fuzz/src/lib.rs` is a finding. A find gets a fix and a hand-written regression test: fuzzer inputs stay out of this repo and out of its logs.
